text:
Maria (Design): quick 10m on the model-pool form — noticed validation feels noisy when people paste lots of fields. do we prefer a single prioritized error + subtle field hints, or the full inline list? :thinking_face:
Noah (PM): depends on mental model. for first-time setups, explicit inline errors help. for power-users doing bulk edits, a single summary + anchors is nicer. can we detect "bulk" mode and switch?
Priya (Eng): we can, but adds complexity. simpler: always show a concise top summary with counts + show the first N inline errors (1-2) and collapse the rest behind a "Show all" toggle. keeps page stable and still surfacess problems.
Jia L: accessibility note: if we collapse errors behind a toggle, ensure the toggle is keyboard-focusable and the expanded list gets focus when opened. use `aria-expanded` state and `aria-controls` to link. also the top summary should be `role="status"` so screen readers get it on submit.
Samir: UX tradeoff: prioritization logic needs rules. proposal: 1) required field errors first, 2) format errors next, 3) warnings last. show severity badges inline (error/warning). this helps users triage.
Maria (Design): love severity badges. copy question: do we say "Required" on label vs `*`? earlier threads argued asterisk + sr-only text. thoughts?
Noah (PM): go with `*` visually to save space, but include `(required)` in the accessible label. also include optional fields with the word "optional" rather than nothing. reduces guesswork.
Priya (Eng): technical nit: if label text becomes "Email * (required)" it might duplicate for screen readers. best is: visible label = "Email *" and programmatically append `aria-label="Email, required"`. that avoids visible clutter.
Jia L: yes. and don't rely on color — make sure the asterisk contrast passes AA.
aria-bot: accessibility checklist suggestion: [1] `role=status` on top summary, [2] `aria-invalid` on invalid inputs, [3] `aria-describedby` linking helper/error text, [4] keyboard-focusable error list toggle.
Maria (Design): destructive action inside form: example is "Remove linked credential" button inline. typed-confirm seems heavy; prefer inline modal + undo toast for these. typed-confirm reserved for account-level destruction. what about wording?
Samir: modal primary CTA should be explicit: "Remove credential" vs "Remove". include one line about consequences. then show an undo toast: "Credential removed — Undo" that lasts 8s and is keyboard accessible.
Priya (Eng): implementational detail: undo should re-add the object client-side with a server-side TTL to allow replay; otherwise users hit inconsistent state if network fails.
Noah (PM): good call. copy for the modal body: "This will unlink the credential from your pool. This does not delete the credential itself. You can undo this action from the toast for 8 seconds." any shorter variants?
Maria (Design): shorter: "Unlink credential from pool. You can undo this action." add a link to docs for edgecases. primary CTA: "Unlink credential"; secondary: "Cancel". add `aria-describedby` to explain undo window.
Jia L: accessibility/keyboard: modal focus trap, initial focus on close button or the cancel? recommend initial focus on the modal heading, then tabbable primary CTA last so keyboard users read consequences first. also ensure screen reader announces short consequence text on open.
Samir: last thing: visual density — propose collapsing helper text by default and showing an inline chevron to expand help per-field. small animation. keeps vertical rhythm.
Priya (Eng): agree, but ensure expansion state is preserved if form validation fails and we jump to a field. otherwise user loses context.
Maria (Design): action items: - mock two variants (summary-first with prioritized inline + "show all" toggle; per-field collapsed helpers with severity badges) - write copy snippets for modals/toasts - accessibility checklist (aria attributes, focus rules, SR copy) - implementation notes for undo TTL and state preservation.
Noah (PM): ETA for mocks + copy?
Maria (Design): I'll upload mocks by EOD tomorrow and post here. will include redlines for engineering.
Priya (Eng): ping for dev review after mock upload. I'll review the aria attrs and undo logic.
Samir: thanks everyone. small thumbs up if you're good with the approach. :thumbsup: :eyes:
